title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous page. S is a graded ring and 𝓜 is the category of graded S-modules. τ_N M = M_{≥N} is truncation. A module M is N-negligible if τ_N M = 0. It is ∞-negligible if it is N-negligible for some N. It is negligible if every element is killed by some τ_N S, i.e. M is torsion for the irrelevant ideal. There is a chain Nég_N ⊂ Nég_∞ ⊂ Nég of thick subcategories, with Serre quotients 𝓜_N = 𝓜/Nég_N and 𝓜_ω = 𝓜/Nég. The functors τ_N : 𝓜 → 𝓜_N and τ_ω : 𝓜 → 𝓜_ω are the localization functors, and φ_N, φ_ω are their right adjoints (section functors). 𝓜_ω is the Serre/Gabriel model of quasi-coherent sheaves on Proj S, and φ_ωτ_ω P is the analogue of Γ_*(P~).

This page proves that the canonical map lim_N φ_Nτ_N P → φ_ωτ_ω P is an isomorphism.
1. To test bijectivity it suffices to apply Hom(M, –) for M of finite presentation. In fact the free modules M = S[i] suffice, since Hom(S[i], X) is a graded component of X.
2. For such M, Hom(M, –) commutes with the filtered colimit. So the left side becomes lim Hom(M, φ_Nτ_N P) = lim Hom_{𝓜_N}(τ_N M, τ_N P) = lim_N Hom_𝓜(τ_N M, P).
3. The right side is Hom_{𝓜_ω}(τ_ω M, τ_ω P). By Gabriel's description of Hom in a Serre quotient this is lim over M' ⊂ M with M/M' negligible of Hom(M', P).
4. So, for M fixed, the map is an isomorphism for all P as soon as the two systems of subobjects {τ_N M} and {M' ⊂ M : M/M' negligible} are mutually cofinal. That is, every M' with negligible quotient must contain some τ_N M.
5. This holds when M is of finite type: M/M' is then of finite type and negligible, hence killed by some τ_N S, hence ∞-negligible.
6. A crossed-out attempt tries to generalize to any ideal J of S with S/J negligible.

Conclusion: lim_N φ_Nτ_N P ≅ φ_ωτ_ω P. This is the module-theoretic form of Γ_*(Proj S, P~) = lim_N Hom(S_{≥N}, P), here as a lemma inside the 1976 notes on the divided-power de Rham complex, where S is presumably a symmetric or divided-power algebra.
errors: Gabriel's formula for Hom in 𝓜/Nég is lim over pairs (M' ⊂ M, P' ⊂ P) with M/M' and P' negligible of Hom(M', P/P'). The page drops the P' (torsion of P) part. This is harmless when P has no negligible submodules. In general it needs an extra argument, e.g. vanishing of lim_N Ext^1(τ_N M, T) for torsion T, which holds when S is noetherian.

Unstated hypotheses. Step 5 needs that a finite-type negligible module is killed by some τ_N S. It also needs τ_N S·M and M_{≥N'} to be mutually cofinal, which requires S to be finitely generated in positive degrees (and, for the torsion point, noetherian). These conditions are only implicit.
Mixing f.p. M with 'il suffit M = S[i]' is slightly redundant but not wrong.

ideas.what: Graded modules modulo negligible (irrelevant-ideal torsion) modules as a model of QCoh(Proj S); tower of quotients 𝓜/Nég_N
ideas.modern_name: Serre's theorem / Serre quotient description of Proj; tails category (Artin–Zhang)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (FAC 1955), Gabriel (1962), later Artin–Zhang (1994) for noncommutative Proj
ideas.where_published: EGA II §2.7 and EGA III §2 (Γ_* and the comparison with graded modules up to torsion)

ideas.what: Section functor of the Proj quotient as the colimit of the section functors of the truncation quotients: lim φ_Nτ_N P ≅ φ_ωτ_ω P
ideas.modern_name: Γ_*(P~) = lim_N Hom(S_{≥N}, P) (ideal transform / Deligne formula)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre FAC; Gabriel; Deligne's formula in SGA4 / Hartshorne Residues and Duality
ideas.where_published: EGA II 2.7 / EGA I (1971) style statements on Γ_* and colimits of Hom from ideals

ideas.what: Cofinality of {τ_N M} among subobjects with negligible quotient for M of finite type

deep.surprise_reason: A routine, correct-up-to-hypotheses verification of the standard Serre/Gabriel description of sections on Proj via colimits over truncations. The stratified quotient tower 𝓜/Nég_N is mildly nice bookkeeping but is standard in tails-category literature.
transcription_corrections: '(dire que ceci, M fixé)' reads better as '(dire que ceci, M fixé, est un iso pour tout P, signifie que les deux systèmes de sous-modules de M, soit des τ_N M, soit des M' ⊂ M tels que M/M' est négligeable, sont équivalents pour l'ordre, ou encore que ces deux systèmes de sous-objets sont cofinaux)'.
The crossed-out passage is roughly '[Plus généralement] quel que soit l'idéal J de S tel que S/J soit négligeable', with the margin note 'M/JM' or 'M/J' ('Mais c'est le cas si M de type fini').
The '[-Hom-]' at the top is a crossed-out word to the left of 'bijectif?'.
